profile.name: home
profile.description: Comprehensive Windows 11 security profile for home and workstation systems (Antivirus, File Security, Persistence, Network, and System Hardening)

controls.title: Windows Firewall active on all profiles
controls.description: Verifies that Windows Defender Firewall is enabled across Domain, Private, and Public profiles with DefaultInboundAction set to Block.
controls.rationale: The firewall is the first line of defense against unauthorized inbound connections. Disabling it exposes the system to network-based attacks.

controls.title: UAC (User Account Control) enabled
controls.description: Verifies that User Account Control (UAC) is enabled via the EnableLUA registry value.
controls.rationale: UAC protects the operating system by prompting before elevated administrative operations. Disabling it allows any program to run with administrative privileges silently.

controls.title: UAC prompts for elevation on Secure Desktop
controls.description: Verifies that UAC requires elevation consent (ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin in 1, 2, 5) on the Secure Desktop (PromptOnSecureDesktop = 1).
controls.rationale: If UAC does not prompt on the Secure Desktop, malicious processes can intercept or spoof confirmation dialogs to gain administrative privileges.

controls.title: UAC detects application installations
controls.description: Verifies that UAC detects application installers and prompts for elevation (EnableInstallerDetection = 1).
controls.rationale: Installer detection helps prevent unauthorized software installations from running silently without user consent.

controls.title: Guest account disabled
controls.description: Verifies that the built-in local Guest account (SID ending in -501) is disabled.
controls.rationale: The Guest account allows anonymous local access to the system. If enabled, anyone can sign in without credentials.

controls.title: Built-in local Administrator account disabled
controls.description: Verifies that the built-in local Administrator account (SID ending in -500) is disabled.
controls.rationale: The built-in Administrator account is a common target for brute-force attacks. Using a dedicated personal administrative account is more secure.

controls.title: No active local account without a password
controls.description: Verifies that all enabled local accounts require a password (PasswordRequired = True), excluding Microsoft Account / Windows Hello managed accounts.
controls.rationale: Accounts without passwords allow anyone with physical or network access to log in without authentication.

controls.title: Automatic Windows Updates enabled
controls.description: Verifies that the Windows Update service (wuauserv) is not disabled and the NoAutoUpdate policy is not active.
controls.rationale: Security updates patch known vulnerabilities. Disabling automatic updates leaves the system exposed to exploitation.

controls.title: Official Windows Update server (no WSUS hijacking)
controls.description: Verifies that Windows Updates are not redirected to an unauthorized external WSUS server (WUServer).
controls.rationale: Malware can configure a rogue WSUS update server to block official Microsoft security patches or serve malicious payloads.

controls.title: Real-time antivirus protection active
controls.description: Verifies that Windows Defender real-time protection is enabled.
controls.rationale: Real-time protection inspects files on access and blocks known threats before they can execute.

controls.title: Antivirus signatures up to date
controls.description: Verifies that Windows Defender antivirus signatures were updated within the last 7 days.
controls.rationale: Outdated antivirus signatures fail to detect recently discovered malware and exploit kits.

controls.title: No active virus or malware threats detected by Defender
controls.description: Queries Windows Defender threat catalog (Get-MpThreat / Get-MpThreatDetection) to ensure no active viruses or unresolved malware detections exist.
controls.rationale: Active threats indicate an ongoing infection or a malicious file that has not yet been quarantined or removed.

controls.title: Downloaded file scanning (IOAV) and behavior monitoring active
controls.description: Verifies that BehaviorMonitorEnabled and IoavProtectionEnabled are active in Windows Defender.
controls.rationale: IOAV protection automatically scans all browser downloads and email attachments, while behavior monitoring blocks ransomware and suspicious process activity.

controls.title: Potentially Unwanted Application (PUA) blocking enabled
controls.description: Verifies that PUAProtection is set to 1 (Enabled / Block) in Windows Defender preferences.
controls.rationale: PUA protection blocks adware, cryptominers, intrusive toolbars, and unwanted bundled software downloaded from the Internet.

controls.title: Tamper Protection and Cloud-delivered protection (MAPS) active
controls.description: Verifies that IsTamperProtected is True and MAPSReporting (Cloud Protection) is enabled.
controls.rationale: Tamper Protection prevents malware from disabling Windows Defender via registry or commands, while Cloud MAPS helps block zero-day threats.

controls.title: Periodic antivirus scan completed within the last 14 days
controls.description: Verifies that a Quick or Full Windows Defender scan has completed within the last 14 days.
controls.rationale: Periodic scans detect dormant threats written to disk prior to the latest signature updates.

controls.title: No dangerous folder or extension exclusions in Defender
controls.description: Verifies that entire drives (C:\), user directories (Downloads, Temp, Windows), or executable extensions (.exe, .ps1, .bat) are not excluded from antivirus scanning.
controls.rationale: Trojans and infostealers frequently add broad paths or executable extensions to Defender exclusions to evade detection.
references: MITRE ATT&CK T1562.001 - Disable or Modify Tools

controls.title: No disguised double-extension executables (Downloads, Desktop, Temp)
controls.description: Performs a read-only scan of Downloads, Desktop, and Temp folders for disguised double-extension executables (e.g., invoice.pdf.exe, photo.jpg.scr, doc.txt.vbs).
controls.rationale: Double extensions are a common masquerading technique used to trick users into executing malware disguised as PDF documents or images.
references: MITRE ATT&CK T1036.007 - Double File Extension

controls.title: No suspicious or obfuscated entries in Startup Run keys
controls.description: Inspects HKCU/HKLM Run and RunOnce registry startup keys for executables launching from Temp directories or obfuscated PowerShell/script commands.
controls.rationale: Malware commonly achieves persistence via Run keys pointing to temporary folders or using hidden/encoded commands (-w hidden, -enc, mshta, wscript).
references: MITRE ATT&CK T1547.001 - Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder

controls.title: Windows hosts file integrity (no hijacked security domains)
controls.description: Inspects C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts to verify that Windows Update, Microsoft, or antivirus vendor domains are not blocked or redirected.
controls.rationale: Malware modifies the hosts file to block security updates and prevent access to antivirus vendor websites.
references: MITRE ATT&CK T1565.001 - Stored Data Manipulation

controls.title: Known file extensions visible in File Explorer
controls.description: Verifies that HideFileExt is set to 0 in HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Advanced.
controls.rationale: Always displaying file extensions in File Explorer allows users to immediately identify executable files (.exe, .scr, .bat) disguised as documents.
references: CIS Benchmark Windows 11 - User Explorer Settings

controls.title: AutoRun and AutoPlay disabled for removable USB drives
controls.description: Verifies that automatic execution when inserting USB drives or external media is disabled (NoDriveTypeAutoRun >= 145 or DisableAutoplay = 1).
controls.rationale: Disabling AutoRun and AutoPlay prevents malware on infected USB drives from executing automatically upon insertion.

controls.title: Microsoft Defender SmartScreen enabled for apps and files
controls.description: Verifies that SmartScreen is active for File Explorer and web content evaluation (EnableWebContentEvaluation).
controls.rationale: SmartScreen warns users before running unrecognized or potentially malicious applications downloaded from the Internet.

controls.title: Core Isolation / Memory Integrity (HVCI) active
controls.description: Verifies that Hypervisor-Enforced Code Integrity (HVCI) is actively running via Win32_DeviceGuard runtime state.
controls.rationale: Memory Integrity uses hardware virtualization to prevent malicious code injection into high-security Windows kernel processes.

controls.title: Anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts restricted
controls.description: Verifies that RestrictAnonymousSAM in HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa is set to 1.
controls.rationale: Prevents unauthenticated users on the local network from enumerating local account names on the system.

controls.title: Remote Desktop (RDP) disabled
controls.description: Verifies that Remote Desktop (RDP) is disabled via fDenyTSConnections = 1.
controls.rationale: RDP is one of the most frequently targeted attack vectors. If remote desktop access is not required, it should remain disabled.

controls.title: SMBv1 protocol disabled
controls.description: Verifies that the legacy SMBv1 protocol is disabled.
controls.rationale: SMBv1 has critical known vulnerabilities (EternalBlue/WannaCry). Modern SMBv2/SMBv3 protocols should be used instead.

controls.title: NetBIOS over TCP/IP disabled
controls.description: Verifies that NetBIOS over TCP/IP is disabled (NetbiosOptions = 2) on network interfaces.
controls.rationale: NetBIOS exposes host information and enables name-resolution spoofing attacks on local networks. It should be disabled when not required.

controls.title: LLMNR multicast name resolution disabled
controls.description: Verifies that Link-Local Multicast Name Resolution (EnableMulticast = 0) is disabled.
controls.rationale: LLMNR is vulnerable to poisoning attacks (such as Responder) on local and public Wi-Fi networks, allowing attackers to capture NTLMv2 password hashes.

controls.title: BitLocker or Device Encryption active on system drive
controls.description: Verifies that BitLocker or Windows Device Encryption is enabled on the system partition (C:).
controls.rationale: Full-disk encryption protects sensitive data at rest in the event of physical theft or loss of the device.

controls.title: Windows telemetry set to minimum level
controls.description: Verifies that Windows telemetry (AllowTelemetry) is configured to the minimum permitted level (<= 1).
controls.rationale: Minimizing telemetry limits the amount of diagnostic and usage data collected and transmitted to Microsoft.

controls.title: UEFI Secure Boot active
controls.description: Verifies that Secure Boot is enabled in UEFI firmware.
controls.rationale: Secure Boot prevents unsigned bootloaders from loading at startup, defending against rootkits and bootkits.

controls.title: LSA Protection (RunAsPPL) enabled
controls.description: Verifies that Local Security Authority (LSA) Protection (RunAsPPL) is enabled.
controls.rationale: LSA Protection blocks non-protected processes from injecting into LSASS and dumping credentials from memory (e.g., Mimikatz).

controls.title: PowerShell Script Block Logging enabled
controls.description: Verifies that PowerShell Script Block Logging (EnableScriptBlockLogging) is enabled.
controls.rationale: Script Block Logging records executed PowerShell code blocks in the Windows Event Log, aiding detection of suspicious or obfuscated scripts.

controls.title: Ransomware protection (Controlled Folder Access) enabled
controls.description: Verifies that Windows Defender Controlled Folder Access (EnableControlledFolderAccess = 1) is enabled.
controls.rationale: Controlled Folder Access prevents ransomware and untrusted applications from encrypting or modifying protected personal directories (Documents, Pictures, Desktop).
references: Microsoft Defender Exploit Guard - Controlled Folder Access

controls.title: Microsoft Defender Network Protection (Exploit Guard) active
controls.description: Verifies that Microsoft Defender Network Protection (EnableNetworkProtection = 1) is active in Block mode.
controls.rationale: Network Protection blocks outbound connections to known phishing domains, malware C2 servers, and exploit hosts across all applications and browsers.

controls.title: No suspicious or obfuscated Scheduled Tasks
controls.description: Audits non-Microsoft Scheduled Tasks for executions from Temp/Public folders or obfuscated PowerShell/LOLBin commands.
controls.rationale: Malware frequently abuses Windows Scheduled Tasks to maintain persistent background execution at logon or on recurring timers.

controls.title: No system executable hijacking (IFEO Debugger Hijacking)
controls.description: Verifies that no critical system or accessibility executable (sethc.exe, utilman.exe, taskmgr.exe, MsMpEng.exe) has a Debugger value in Image File Execution Options.
controls.rationale: Attackers abuse IFEO Debugger hijacking to install login-screen backdoors (Sticky Keys) or block security tools such as Task Manager and Defender.
references: MITRE ATT&CK T1546.012 - Image File Execution Options Injection

controls.title: No suspicious scripts or executables in Startup folders
controls.description: Scans user and system Startup folders for suspicious scripts or executables (.vbs, .js, .bat, .cmd, .ps1, .hta, .scr).
controls.rationale: Any script or executable placed in the Startup folder is automatically launched every time a user signs in.
references: MITRE ATT&CK T1547.001 - Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder

controls.title: Account lockout policy enabled against brute-force attacks
controls.description: Verifies that the Account Lockout Threshold is configured between 1 and 10 failed logon attempts.
controls.rationale: Without an account lockout threshold, an attacker or malware on the local network can perform unlimited password-guessing attempts.

controls.title: Minimal number of local Administrators group members (<= 2)
controls.description: Verifies that the local Administrators group (SID S-1-5-32-544) contains no more than 2 enabled accounts.
controls.rationale: Minimizing accounts with administrative privileges reduces the attack surface and limits blast radius in the event of account compromise.

controls.title: No non-standard SMB network shares exposed
controls.description: Verifies that no user-defined SMB shares are exposed on the local network beyond default administrative shares.
controls.rationale: Exposed local network shares can be abused by ransomware or untrusted devices on the same Wi-Fi network to read or encrypt files.
references: MITRE ATT&CK T1135 - Network Share Discovery

controls.title: Mandatory SMB digital signing enabled (anti-NTLM Relay)
controls.description: Verifies that RequireSecuritySignature = 1 is enforced for both SMB Server and SMB Client.
controls.rationale: Mandatory SMB packet signing prevents local network attackers from intercepting and relaying credentials via SMB/NTLM Relay attacks.

controls.title: Windows Remote Management (WinRM / PowerShell Remoting) disabled
controls.description: Verifies that the WinRM service is stopped so remote administration ports 5985/5986 are not exposed.
controls.rationale: On personal desktops and laptops, WinRM exposes a remote PowerShell execution endpoint frequently abused for lateral movement.

controls.title: WPAD automatic web proxy discovery disabled (anti-MITM)
controls.description: Verifies that Web Proxy Auto-Discovery (WPAD) is disabled in the registry or via the WinHttpAutoProxySvc service.
controls.rationale: An attacker on the same LAN or Wi-Fi network can spoof WPAD responses to intercept and proxy all web traffic from the machine.

controls.title: WDigest credential protection (no cleartext passwords in memory)
controls.description: Anti-tampering check verifying that WDigest UseLogonCredential is set to 0 (or absent) to prevent cleartext password caching in LSASS.
controls.rationale: If an attacker sets WDigest UseLogonCredential to 1, Windows caches user passwords in plaintext in RAM, enabling credential theft.

controls.title: Windows Remote Assistance disabled
controls.description: Verifies that fAllowToGetHelp is set to 0 in the Remote Assistance registry key.
controls.rationale: Disabling Remote Assistance reduces the risk of unauthorized remote support connections to the computer.

controls.title: Remote Registry service disabled
controls.description: Verifies that the RemoteRegistry service is disabled (Start = 4) and not running.
controls.rationale: The Remote Registry service allows remote reading and modification of the Windows registry over the network.

controls.title: Microsoft Vulnerable Driver Blocklist (anti-BYOVD) enabled
controls.description: Verifies that Microsoft's Vulnerable Driver Blocklist (VulnerableDriverBlocklistEnable = 1) is enabled in CI\Config.
controls.rationale: Prevents loading signed drivers with known vulnerabilities abused in Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver (BYOVD) attacks to disable EDR/Defender in the kernel.
references: Microsoft Security Baseline Windows 11 - Driver Block Rules
MITRE ATT&CK T1068 - Exploitation for Privilege Escalation (BYOVD)

controls.title: Smart App Control (SAC) active
controls.description: Verifies Smart App Control status (VerifiedAndReputablePolicyState = 1 Enforced or 2 Evaluation) in Control\CI\Policy.
controls.rationale: Smart App Control blocks untrusted, unsigned, or potentially malicious applications at the OS level on Windows 11.
references: Microsoft Windows 11 Security - Smart App Control

controls.title: Microsoft Defender Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rules active
controls.description: Verifies via Get-MpPreference that ASR rules are configured in Block (1) or Warn (6) mode, including LSASS credential theft protection and obfuscated script blocking.
controls.rationale: ASR rules block common ransomware and fileless malware techniques such as LSASS credential dumping, malicious Office macros, and obfuscated scripts.
references: Microsoft Defender Exploit Guard - Attack Surface Reduction

controls.title: Hardware security chip TPM 2.0 present and ready
controls.description: Verifies via Get-Tpm (or Win32_Tpm) that a TPM 2.0 module is present and ready for use (TpmPresent = True, TpmReady = True).
controls.rationale: TPM 2.0 provides the hardware root of trust required by BitLocker, Windows Hello, Secure Boot, and Credential Guard.
references: Microsoft Windows 11 Hardware Security Baseline - TPM 2.0

controls.title: Legacy TLS 1.0/1.1 disabled and DNS over HTTPS (DoH) supported
controls.description: Verifies that TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 are not forced enabled in SCHANNEL and that the DNS client supports DNS over HTTPS (DoH).
controls.rationale: Disabling TLS 1.0/1.1 prevents cryptographic downgrade attacks (BEAST/POODLE), while DNS over HTTPS encrypts DNS queries against interception and spoofing.
references: IETF RFC 8996 - Deprecating TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1
IETF RFC 8484 - DNS Queries over HTTPS (DoH)

controls.title: Windows Script Host (WSH) disabled against malicious .vbs/.js scripts
controls.description: Verifies that Windows Script Host (wscript.exe/cscript.exe) is disabled by setting Enabled = 0 in Windows Script Host\Settings.
controls.rationale: Disabling WSH blocks automatic execution of VBScript (.vbs/.vbe) and JScript (.js/.jse) droppers commonly delivered via phishing campaigns.

controls.title: Secure PowerShell ExecutionPolicy (no Unrestricted or Bypass scopes)
controls.description: Verifies via Get-ExecutionPolicy -List that no persistent scope (MachinePolicy, UserPolicy, LocalMachine, CurrentUser) is set to Unrestricted or Bypass.
controls.rationale: An overly permissive ExecutionPolicy allows unsigned or Internet-downloaded PowerShell scripts to run without restriction.

controls.title: Windows 11 Administrator Protection (JIT) active
controls.description: Verifies that Windows 11 24H2/25H2/26H2 just-in-time Administrator Protection is enabled via TypeOfAdminApprovalMode = 2 in Policies\System.
controls.rationale: Administrator Protection creates a separate hidden admin account with just-in-time elevation tokens, preventing malware from silently inheriting a standing admin token.
references: Microsoft Security Baseline Windows 11 25H2/26H2 - Administrator Protection

controls.title: No fileless persistence via WMI Event Subscriptions
controls.description: Queries the root\subscription namespace in read-only mode to ensure no suspicious CommandLineEventConsumer, ActiveScriptEventConsumer, or EventFilter objects exist.
controls.rationale: Attackers abuse permanent WMI event subscriptions to achieve stealthy fileless persistence outside standard Run keys, executing scripts or commands on system events.
references: MITRE ATT&CK T1546.003 - Windows Management Instrumentation Event Subscription

controls.title: No policy-forced browser extensions (Chrome / Edge)
controls.description: Verifies that ExtensionInstallForcelist registry keys in HKLM/HKCU for Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge do not contain forced extensions.
controls.rationale: Malware, adware, and infostealers often force silent installation of malicious browser extensions via ExtensionInstallForcelist, preventing users from removing them via the browser UI.

controls.title: Windows Event Log integrity and no recent Security log clearing (Event ID 1102)
controls.description: Verifies that the Windows Event Log service (EventLog) is running and queries the Security event log for log-clearing events (Event ID 1102) in the last 30 days.
controls.rationale: Attackers frequently stop the Event Log service or clear the Security log (Event ID 1102) to hide intrusion evidence and evade forensic investigation.
references: MITRE ATT&CK T1070.001 - Clear Windows Event Logs
CIS Benchmark Windows 11 - Event Log Service

controls.title: PrintNightmare printer driver installation protection enabled
controls.description: Verifies that the Print Spooler service is disabled or that Point and Print driver installation is not overridden via RestrictDriverInstallationToAdministrators = 0.
controls.rationale: Allowing non-administrators to install printer drivers via Point and Print exposes Windows to PrintNightmare (CVE-2021-34527) local privilege escalation and remote code execution.

controls.title: No vulnerable unquoted service executable paths
controls.description: Audits registered Windows services (Win32_Service) for third-party executable paths containing spaces that are not enclosed in quotation marks.
controls.rationale: Unquoted service paths containing spaces outside SystemRoot allow local privilege escalation by placing a malicious executable earlier in Windows path resolution order.
references: MITRE ATT&CK T1574.009 - Path Interception by Unquoted Path

controls.title: Kernel DMA Protection enabled against external PCIe/Thunderbolt attacks
controls.description: Queries Win32_DeviceGuard AvailableSecurityProperties for hardware Kernel DMA Protection support and verifies it is not disabled via DeviceEnumerationPolicy = 2.
controls.rationale: Kernel DMA Protection leverages hardware IOMMU isolation to block rogue external PCIe or Thunderbolt peripherals from performing unauthorized direct memory access.
references: Microsoft Secured-core PC - Kernel DMA Protection

controls.title: No insecure Wi-Fi profiles configured for AutoConnect
controls.description: Parses saved WLAN XML profiles under C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Wlansvc\Profiles\Interfaces in read-only mode to ensure no open, shared, WEP, WPA, WPAPSK, or TKIP network is configured with connectionMode set to auto.
controls.rationale: Automatic connection to open, WEP, or legacy WPA/TKIP wireless networks exposes traffic to passive eavesdropping and Evil Twin / Adversary-in-the-Middle attacks whenever an attacker broadcasts a matching SSID.
references: NIST SP 800-153 - Guidelines for Securing Wireless Local Area Networks

controls.title: No high-risk TCP ports exposed on all network interfaces
controls.description: Inspects listening TCP sockets via Get-NetTCPConnection (excluding loopback addresses and RPC port 135) to verify that high-risk remote-access, legacy, or backdoor ports (21, 23, 69, 139, 1433, 3389, 4444, 5900, 5985, 5986, 6379) are not exposed.
controls.rationale: Unrestricted remote-administration, unencrypted legacy, or database TCP services bound to non-loopback interfaces significantly expand the network attack surface for brute-force, lateral movement, and exploitation.
